reviews.mechanism: Gzip recovery appends already-consumed buffer bytes; the after slice retains a zero-size replay boundary.

reviews.contract_reason: The old local doc promises as much decompressed data as possible despite CRC errors. Retained CPython2.7.12 read semantics keep consumed bytes in extrabuf while extrasize tracks unread bytes, so copying the full buffer can duplicate output. The repair narrows the suffix only when extrasize is positive.

A footer-truncated stream whose decompressed payload is an exact multiple of 8196 can have all buffered output consumed before the next CRC/length read fails; extrasize=0 with a retained nonempty extrabuf then replays its consumed bytes. This is a source-deduced residual old failure, not a demonstrated newly introduced regression.
